## Details

### `show dvr members [controller | leaf]`

A leaf that is missing has no fabric connectivity to the controllers, or has a different domain ID.


### `show dvr host-entries [ipv4 <ip> | l2isid <isid> | vrf <vrf>]`

```
show dvr host-entries ipv4 10.10.100.25
show dvr host-entries vrf CORP
```

The type is 1 for local and 2 for dynamic (learned from another node). Shows the node behind which the host was learned.


### `dvr controller <domain-id>`

Prerequisites are IP shortcuts (`spbm 1 ip enable`) and the dvr-leaf-mode boot flag disabled. A controller belongs to exactly one domain.

> ▲ **Caution:** Removing DvR from a controller deletes the domain and everything learned dynamically.


### `boot config flags dvr-leaf-mode / dvr leaf <domain-id>`

```
save config
boot config flags dvr-leaf-mode
dvr leaf 5
save config
reset -y
```

> ▲ **Caution:** Enabling the dvr-leaf-mode flag removes all non-DvR config such as platform VLAN IPs, CLIPs, routing protocols and VRFs. Save a backup first.


### `dvr gw-ipv4 <gateway-ip> / dvr enable`

```
vlan create 200 type port-mstprstp 0
vlan i-sid 200 20200
interface vlan 200
  vrf CORP
  dvr gw-ipv4 10.20.0.1
  dvr enable
  ip address 10.20.0.2 255.255.255.0
```

The VLAN must have an I-SID. Use the same gateway IP on all controllers of the domain; each controller gets its own VLAN IP. To save addresses, make the VLAN IP the same as the gateway IP (`ip address <ip/len> dvr-one-ip`).


### `dvr redistribute direct enable / dvr apply redistribute [vrf <vrf>]`

Like IS-IS redistribution, nothing happens until you run `dvr apply redistribute`. Check it with `show dvr redistribute`.


### `ip anycast-gateway <gateway-ip> [vrid <1-255>] / ip anycast-gateway enable`

```
interface vlan 300
  ip address 10.30.0.2/24
  ip anycast-gateway 10.30.0.1
  ip anycast-gateway enable
```

The gateway IP (and the vrid, which defines the gateway MAC) must match on every router of the same L2 VSN. `ip anycast-gateway one-ip <ip/len>` uses one address for VLAN IP and gateway. Since 9.2 the switch logs when a client spoofs the gateway IP on an access port.
